tools.name: check_address
tools.description: Check whether a crypto address is at risk of a USDT (Tether) freeze or is already frozen. Covers Ethereum, Tron, Avalanche, Celo, Solana and TON. Returns risk level 0–3 (0 no risk, 1 freeze proposal open in Tether multisig, 2 second of three signatures collected, 3 blacklisted), recommended action,

tools.name: check_addresses
tools.description: Check up to 20 addresses at once for USDT freeze risk (database check without live node calls). Returns level 0–3, label and action for each address, sorted by risk. Use for screening payout lists, deposit addresses or CSV exports.

tools.name: get_freeze_statistics
tools.description: Current statistics of the USDT blacklist across all chains: number of blacklisted addresses, frozen USDT, freezes in the last 24 h / 30 days, open freeze proposals, median delay from proposal to freeze by chain, delay distribution and monthly dynamics for the last 12 months.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search LIGHTHOUSE knowledge: pass a crypto address to get its freeze-risk record, or keywords (risk levels, how Tether freezes work, coverage, statistics, pricing, API/MCP access). Returns result ids for the fetch tool.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch the full text of a search result by id (address:<address>, doc:<name> or stats:overview).

tools.name: list_open_proposals
tools.description: List freeze (addBlackList) and unfreeze proposals that are open in Tether multisigs but not yet executed — the early-warning signal before an address is frozen. Each item has address, chain, signatures collected/required, age, probability of execution within 10 min and 1 h, and USDT amount at risk.

tools.name: list_recent_freezes
tools.description: Log of executed blacklist operations, newest first: freezes (add), unfreezes (rem) or fund destructions (des), with address, chain, time, delay from proposal and amount. Requires sign-in.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Show the signed-in user's LIGHTHOUSE plan, expiry dates, monitoring subscription and how many addresses are monitored. Requires sign-in.

tools.name: watchlist_list
tools.description: List the user's addresses on LIGHTHOUSE monitoring with their current risk level, last check time and last level change. Requires sign-in.

tools.name: watchlist_add
tools.description: Put an address on LIGHTHOUSE monitoring (up to 10 per account). Risk is re-checked every 10 minutes and right after Tether multisig events; the user gets a Telegram or e-mail notification when the level changes. Requires sign-in and an active monitoring subscription or LIGHTHOUSE plan.

tools.name: watchlist_remove
tools.description: Remove an address from the user's LIGHTHOUSE monitoring list. Requires sign-in.

tools.name: get_plans
tools.description: List LIGHTHOUSE paid plans (API key with dashboard, webhooks and monitoring; or address monitoring only), prices in USDT and accepted crypto payment methods: USDT TRC-20 on Tron (always) and x402 USDC on Base (if enabled). Address checks are free; buy a plan when you need the REST API at scale, open

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Create an order for a LIGHTHOUSE plan paid in crypto. payment_method=usdt_trc20 (default): returns the Tron address and the exact USDT amount (unique cents identify the order), valid 60 minutes; after sending, call submit_payment with the tx hash, then get_order returns the API key. payment_method=x

tools.name: submit_payment
tools.description: After sending USDT TRC-20 for an order, pass the order_id and the Tron transaction hash. The service finds the transfer on-chain, checks recipient and exact amount and, once confirmed (~1 minute), issues or extends the API key. Returns a verdict: paid, unconfirmed, wrong_amount, wrong_recipient or n

tools.name: get_order
tools.description: Get the status of a LIGHTHOUSE order (pending, paid, expired). When paid, returns the API key (for api plans) or the monitoring expiry (for watch plans). Checks incoming transfers on each call.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "create_order" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
